sb_prompt: WHAT KIND OF DINING OUT DO YOU ENJOY? WHAT THINGS DO YOU LOOK FOR IN A RESTAURANT THAT WOULD GET YOU TO GO BACK AGAIN?  SEE WHETHER THE OTHER CALLER'S PREFERENCES ARE SIMILAR TO YOURS.
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hey there.
ParticipantB: Hi.
ParticipantA: Yeah, we were supposed to talk about restaurants today.
ParticipantB: Right, the restaurants thing.
ParticipantA: Well, I don't really know about that. I mostly just eat at the diner down the street.
ParticipantB: Oh, the one with the neon sign? Yeah, that's my place too.
ParticipantA: Right. It's got cheap food and no fuss.
ParticipantB: Yeah, the nice place doesn't seem like much if you just want to fill up.
ParticipantA: True. I had a car come in last week with a blown head gasket.
ParticipantB: Oh yeah?
ParticipantA: So I fixed it, and then the guy came back three days later saying I couldn't have messed that up.
ParticipantB: That sounds suspicious.
ParticipantA: Yeah, kind of made me think twice about trusting anyone who tells you everything is fine.
ParticipantB: Huh. That's a good point. I think people like that are trying to sell you something extra.
ParticipantA: Yeah, probably. But I guess when you need a meal, you just want it done right.
ParticipantB: Right. I used to go to these fancy places all the time, you know, like the steakhouse downtown.
ParticipantA: Oh, the one with the live jazz?
ParticipantB: Yeah, that one. But lately I just don't go there.
ParticipantA: Why not?
ParticipantB: Well, I went there last year and my wife and I shared a dessert and it cost like thirty bucks.
ParticipantA: Thirty bucks for two slices of cake?
ParticipantB: Yeah. And the coffee was lukewarm. So I just stopped going.
ParticipantA: That makes sense. I can't afford that kind of stuff anyway.
ParticipantB: Yeah, exactly. I figured out years ago that I'm better off cooking at home.
ParticipantA: Oh, you cook?
ParticipantB: Yeah, simple stuff. Maybe a stir-fry or a roast. Saves a lot of money.
ParticipantA: That's smart. I should try that more often.
ParticipantB: You should. It's healthier too, mostly.
ParticipantA: Yeah, sure. I guess I just like the place where I can get what I want without the attitude.
ParticipantB: Exactly. No pretension, no upselling. Just food.
ParticipantA: Right. That's what matters.
ParticipantB: Yeah. Well, I think that covers it.
ParticipantA: Me too. Thanks for chatting.
ParticipantB: Bye.
